text: The bombing may have paused, but the missile war has not. For three days, the US strikes on Iran have stopped. But Tehran's retaliatory fire has kept the pressure on, exposing the challenge of stopping missiles designed to confuse even sophisticated air defences. And one Iranian weapon is now drawing particular attention. The Khyber Shekham.

The bombs have stopped falling, for now. After two weeks of relentless US bombardment, Washington has paused its strikes on Iran. Tehran, too, has halted its missile and drone attacks on American bases. But Tehran's retaliation has stunned America. Iranian missiles and drones have kept targeting American positions, forcing US forces to rely heavily on expensive interceptors to defend themselves.
And that is where the Khyber Shekhan enters the picture. The Iranian missile is relatively compact.
It is mobile. It is designed for precision. And its biggest advantage may be the way it flies. According to reports, the Khyber Shekhan can combine different flight paths,
manoeuvres and speeds, making it harder for air defense systems to predict exactly where the missile is heading.

An interceptor has to detect the incoming weapon, calculate its trajectory and destroy it before impact. But if the missile changes its behavior during flight, the window for defense becomes smaller. Iran's strategy is therefore not simply about firing more missiles, it is about making every incoming missile harder to stop. Every Iranian missile or drone forces America to make a choice.
Or fire an interceptor. The problem is that interceptors are expensive and limited.

According to assessments by the Center for Strategic and International Studies, the United States has already used roughly one-third of its combined pre-war inventory of critical precision weapons during early fighting with Iran. These include THAAD, Patriot interceptors, as well as offensive missiles.
Trump, however, dismissed those reports, insisting American stockpiles remain fully loaded.
It does not need to destroy every American defense system. It only needs to overwhelm it,
confuse it and find the gaps and inflict pain.
